mutants.reason: GetStruct runs only after BuildCompiledLayout has resolved every typedef and rejected cycles. A valid alias chain visits distinct declarations and either reaches a non-typedef, returns an inline composite, or stops at a pointer/array alias. It therefore ends before exhausting the declaration count. Admitting one extra iteration at zero cannot affect any constructed layout, lookup result or path error. The count remains bounded and no cyclic layout becomes constructible.

All aliases have already passed ResolveCompiledTypeReference's cycle detection before this query is available. With the unchanged body, GetStruct follows a finite chain of distinct declarations, returns an inline composite, or breaks on a pointer/array/failed lookup. The counter is a redundant defensive bound, not the terminating condition for a supported layout. Incrementing it does not change the declarations visited, returned composite or final path diagnostic; this proof does not apply to the earlier normalization loop that can still see cycles.

On the pointer/array arms of this condition, short-circuiting leaves value equal to the same Typedef. Without break the unchanged declaration counter repeats that same check until zero, then reaches the same 'Declaration is not a struct' exception with the original name. A failed lookup assigns null, so the next while condition stops immediately and produces that same diagnostic. Successful ordinary aliases do not enter this branch. Only redundant bounded lookup work changes; a pointer or array alias never becomes a composite query.

This fallback is guarded by values.Count == 1. The dictionary is the concrete operation-owned StructValue allocated inside ReadResolvedValue or ReadRootValue (or by the compiled engine's root and selected-member reads), not a caller-provided collection; decoding has finished, no callbacks run between the count and enumeration, and the container has not escaped. Its Values enumeration therefore contains exactly one assigned member, including when that member's value is null. Single and SingleOrDefault enumerate that same single member and return it; the empty-sequence behavior on which they differ is unreachable here, and neither sees a second member. This does not qualify removal of the preceding preferred-name fast path: that change adds enumeration storage and is detected by the allocation regression.

TryGetDiagnosticPosition returns nullable Int64. Removing its catch body still swallows the same failed Position query; Stryker 5.0.0 appends its default-return fallback after the try/catch. That fallback returns default(long?), which is null, exactly like the original catch. Successful queries still return the same position. Both forms preserve the primary exception and attach an unavailable offset after a diagnostic failure. Tool implementation: EndingReturnEngine.InjectReturn, https://github.com/stryker-mutator/stryker-net/blob/6e77a3451bac4793e9c839c3ff4055c1b30ca3af/src/Stryker.Core/Stryker.Core/Instrumentation/EndingReturnEngine.cs.

TryGetPosition returns nullable Int64. If querying the source position throws, the original catch returns null. Stryker 5.0.0 makes this block-removal mutant compilable with its default-return fallback; default(long?) is also null. Both paths preserve the original physical-stream exception with no available offset and perform the same single failed position query. Tool implementation: EndingReturnEngine.InjectReturn, https://github.com/stryker-mutator/stryker-net/blob/6e77a3451bac4793e9c839c3ff4055c1b30ca3af/src/Stryker.Core/Stryker.Core/Instrumentation/EndingReturnEngine.cs.

BuildReverseDependents inserts dependent names only from definitionDependencies.Keys, which are exactly definitions.Keys. GetTopologicallySortedDefinitions initializes dependencyCounts with all of those same keys and changes only values, never removes keys. Every dependent reached in this loop is therefore present; the missing-key continue is unreachable.

The graph has one entry per definition and unique dependency edges. A node is queued initially at zero or exactly when its remaining count becomes zero; each node is processed once and counts never become negative. If fewer nodes were ordered than definitions, at least one unresolved cycle node has a positive count. The positive-count predicate therefore always matches here, so First and FirstOrDefault return the same first pair.

BuildCodecTable is private and has two callers. GetSharedCodecTable passes a catalog from PrimitiveCatalog.For (no custom descriptors) and an empty instance array. RegisterCustomCodecs constructs one descriptor and one instance in the same loop; WithCustomCodecs validates and retains every descriptor or throws before BuildCodecTable. Both immutable arrays therefore have identical lengths at this guard. Removing its unreachable throw cannot change supported behavior.

This diagnostic is guarded by different custom descriptor and instance counts. Both private callers construct matching counts: zero for the shared primitive catalog, or one descriptor and instance per registered codec. WithCustomCodecs retains all validated descriptors or throws first. No caller can reach this message with unequal immutable arrays.

ExactEvaluationContext is private, created once for each EvaluateExact call and never reused or exposed. A successful identifier evaluation enters identifierValues before this finally; every later use of that name returns its cached value before consulting activeIdentifiers. During unfinished recursive evaluation the name remains active in both versions, so real cycles are still rejected. If evaluation throws, no exact-interpreter branch catches and resumes it: the whole context is abandoned. Keeping a completed name in the private active set therefore cannot change a value, cycle diagnostic, dependency lookup or depth/work limit. This only retains bookkeeping names until that one evaluation ends; it does not qualify removal from the separately reusable ordinary session.

The SDK emits Enumerable.ToArray<string> for this single HashSet spread, verified in both target assemblies. On supported .NET 8 and .NET 10, ToArray recognizes ICollection<string> and returns Array.Empty<string>() when Count is zero, before CopyTo or enumeration. The dependencies HashSet is private, operation-owned and not mutated after compilation. Thus the empty alternative returns the same shared instance without an allocation or callback; nonempty sets already use the same spread. The shared-empty-storage regression passes on both targets with this exact mutation and guards observable identity.

ExactEvaluationContext is private. EvaluateExact compiles the entire root with GetProgram before entering it, and its EvaluateIdentifier compiles each selected dependency before recursive evaluation. CompileExpression rejects Call nodes in every subtree, even unselected branches. Syntax child references are read-only and cannot change between validation and execution. The exact interpreter's duplicate Call rejection is therefore unreachable; only its message is changed.

The private exact interpreter receives a root only after EvaluateExact calls GetProgram, and receives a dependency only after its own EvaluateIdentifier calls GetProgram. CompileExpression rejects every unsupported node type while traversing the complete immutable tree. Supported expression child references are read-only; their runtime types cannot change after compilation. Thus the exact interpreter's unsupported-node fallback is unreachable, and changing only its prefix cannot alter an observable diagnostic.

Every tree reaching ExactEvaluationContext was first compiled through GetProgram at the root or named-dependency boundary. Compilation's CreateOperatorInstruction rejects all unknown UnaryOperatorType values before exact evaluation starts. UnaryOp.Type and its child reference are read-only, so the checked operator cannot become invalid afterward. The exact unary fallback message is unreachable; the earlier compiler diagnostic is unchanged.

The exact interpreter validates roots and named dependencies through GetProgram before evaluating them. CreateOperatorInstruction rejects an unknown BinaryOperatorType during compilation, including in unselected syntax branches. BinaryOp.Type and its child references are read-only, so successful compilation cannot be followed by a newly invalid operator. This changes only the unreachable duplicate exact-interpreter fallback message; compiler failures remain intact.

This exact Boolean is CompilationFrame.EmitOperator, not its Conditional flag. The same immutable frame is created with BranchStage 2, which emits the logical combining operator and patches its target. CompileExpression handles that stage and unconditionally continues before reading EmitOperator. Changing only this otherwise-unused flag cannot alter emitted instructions, patch targets, dependency flags, depth, work or failures.

This exact Boolean is CompilationFrame.EmitOperator, not its Conditional flag. The same immutable frame is created with BranchStage 1, which emits the logical short-circuit jump. CompileExpression handles that stage and unconditionally continues before reading EmitOperator. Changing only this otherwise-unused flag cannot alter emitted instructions, patch targets, dependency flags, depth, work or failures.

This exact Boolean is CompilationFrame.EmitOperator, not its Conditional flag. The same immutable frame is created with BranchStage 5, which emits the conditional join and patches its target. CompileExpression handles that stage and unconditionally continues before reading EmitOperator. Changing only this otherwise-unused flag cannot alter emitted instructions, patch targets, dependency flags, depth, work or failures.

This exact Boolean is CompilationFrame.EmitOperator, not its Conditional flag. The same immutable frame is created with BranchStage 4, which emits the conditional end jump and patches the else target. CompileExpression handles that stage and unconditionally continues before reading EmitOperator. Changing only this otherwise-unused flag cannot alter emitted instructions, patch targets, dependency flags, depth, work or failures.

This exact Boolean is CompilationFrame.EmitOperator, not its Conditional flag. The same immutable frame is created with BranchStage 3, which emits the conditional false-branch jump. CompileExpression handles that stage and unconditionally continues before reading EmitOperator. Changing only this otherwise-unused flag cannot alter emitted instructions, patch targets, dependency flags, depth, work or failures.

CreateOperatorInstruction is private and has exactly two call sites. BranchStage 2 frames are created only for a logical BinaryOp; EmitOperator frames are created only for UnaryOp or non-logical BinaryOp. Both type patterns are handled before the fallback, including their separate invalid-enum failures. Other syntax nodes never reach this helper. Changing only the no-operator fallback message is therefore unobservable.

mutants.replacement:
ExpressionOpcode.Identifier or ExpressionOpcode.Literal or
                ExpressionOpcode.JumpIfFalse and ExpressionOpcode.JumpIfTrue
mutants.reason: This exact pattern change removes only JumpIfFalse/JumpIfTrue from the three-instruction fast-path exclusion. CompileExpression is the sole producer of the private immutable program: logical operators emit their left program, a jump, the right program and a combining operator, so they require at least four instructions. A three-instruction program cannot end in either jump; the unary exclusions and operand validation remain unchanged. The affected match therefore has the same result before any variable lookup or budget accounting.

This exact pattern change removes only Literal and JumpIfFalse from the three-instruction fast-path exclusion because their enum values cannot match simultaneously. CompileExpression emits a leaf as one instruction, never as the final instruction of a three-instruction root. Logical expressions contain at least four instructions and no complete root ends at their intermediate jump. Other exclusions, including all unary operators, remain unchanged; the guard result and every subsequent operation are identical.

This exact pattern change replaces the Identifier-or-Literal subpattern with an impossible intersection. A scalar leaf compiles to exactly one instruction. Every larger compiler-produced program ends in its root operator or conditional Join, never a leaf. The private instruction array cannot be caller-supplied. Thus the removed leaf alternatives are impossible when code.Length is three; all other exclusions and lookup/budget behavior remain unchanged.

The private compiler emits postfix instructions only for known syntax nodes, rejecting calls and unsupported operators first. Scalars push one; unary operations keep their operand; a binary operation follows both complete operands and removes one slot. Logical jumps do not change the static count. A conditional counts its test and both arms, then Jump and Join remove the two surplus entries. Each complete subtree nets one and every emitted prefix retains a positive count. stackSize can therefore never be zero here, so <= 0 and < 0 are equivalent.

The invalid-stack-transition throw is unreachable for CompileExpression's private instruction stream. Structural induction gives a positive count after every prefix: leaves push, unary operators preserve one, binary operators follow two complete operands and remove one, and conditional Jump/Join remove only the test/extra-arm surplus. Unsupported nodes/operators throw before this constructor. Removing only this defensive throw cannot affect accepted syntax or failure behavior.

The invalid-stack-transition diagnostic is unreachable because every emitted prefix of a private compiled program retains at least one stack value. Binary operators follow both operands, unary operators preserve one, and conditional Jump/Join only remove their accounted surplus entries. No API accepts an arbitrary instruction array. Changing this message cannot affect a reachable result.

CompiledExpression receives exactly one complete tree's private postfix instruction array. Every scalar subtree contributes one stack value; unary preserves it, binary combines two into one, short-circuit bookkeeping preserves the same static effect, and conditional bookkeeping subtracts the test and one extra arm. The complete array therefore has final stackSize == 1. Removing the defensive final-count throw is unobservable.

The final static-stack diagnostic cannot be reached: CompileExpression emits one complete tree, each subtree has net stack effect +1, and its binary/conditional bookkeeping combines child results back to one. Callers cannot replace the private instructions. Changing only the message for stackSize != 1 has no effect on valid values or reachable failures.

For nonzero right operands both paths call BigInteger.Remainder with identical operands. For zero, BigInteger.Remainder itself throws the same parameterless DivideByZeroException as the explicit guard. BigInteger.IsZero is a pure value check. Removing that redundant guard changes neither remainder semantics nor the exception type, message or cause; the exact-modulo regression covers a negative remainder and zero failure.

The CompiledExpression constructor receives only CompileExpression's private instruction list. Every Identifier instruction copies the non-null read-only Identifier.Name: the Identifier constructor dereferences its argument before assignment and its star-removal path also returns a non-null string. Caller data cannot construct or edit instructions. The null-name fallback while collecting unconditional references is unreachable, so changing only its message preserves behavior.

A session runs only compiler-produced programs: CompiledExpression.Code, built from CompileExpression's private instruction list, and a slot program's copy of that code with each identifier's key replaced by its slot. Literals and identifiers push one value; unary instructions preserve one; binary instructions combine two operands into one. Logical short-circuit jumps keep the normalized left result or evaluate the right and combine it; conditional jumps consume the test and execute exactly one value-producing arm. By induction each program finishes with one value or throws earlier; an identifier's evaluation returns one value or throws. Removing the defensive count != 1 throw therefore changes no result or failure.

The message belongs to a defensive count != 1 failure. Sessions run only compiler-produced programs (CompiledExpression.Code, or a slot program's copy of it with slots as keys), which preserve one result by structural induction over scalar, unary, binary, short-circuit and conditional expressions; each branch path leaves exactly one value, and a failing operand exits before this check. Caller data cannot supply instructions or alter stack arity, so changing only this unreachable diagnostic has no effect.

Every caller passes the segments after the root of a path with more than one segment: PrepareWrite builds childSegments = segments.Skip(1).ToArray() only when segments.Count > 1 and hands the same private, nonempty array to EnginePrograms.Write (GetPathWriteProgram) and to SelectWrittenPathValue, which the compiled engine's path writes call. ResolveElementPath either throws during traversal or returns writableField on the final segment before the loop increment. No callback can resize the array or change its Count, and there is no other exit from the loop. The post-loop defensive throw is therefore unreachable in supported writes; removing it cannot suppress any reachable path diagnostic. The earlier array-count and missing-index failures remain required and are covered separately.

Every caller (GetPathWriteProgram through EnginePrograms.Write, and SelectWrittenPathValue for the compiled engine's path writes) receives PrepareWrite's childSegments, built only for paths with more than one segment, so at least one child segment is supplied. The private segment array has a fixed positive Count. Each ResolveElementPath invocation throws within traversal or returns its selected field on the last iteration; it cannot reach the post-loop throw containing this string. Changing only that unreachable message does not change errors for invalid fields, indices, pointer traversal or runtime counts.

The production callers - GetPathWriteProgram from the engine selector and SelectWrittenPathValue for both writers' path writes - receive PrepareWrite's childSegments, which exists only for paths of more than one segment and therefore contains at least one element. Within ResolveElementPath every iteration either throws or, at segmentIndex == segments.Count - 1, returns writableField before incrementing. The loop condition is never evaluated at segmentIndex == segments.Count on a reachable invocation, so changing < to <= cannot add an iteration.

This sealed internal stream has no finalizer. Its only production owner is UpdateStreamCore's local using declaration; the instance does not escape, so disposal always requests managed cleanup and no operation writes after disposal. The first Dispose(true) enters the same body. On completion chunks is null or empty and rangeBytes is null; a repeated Dispose(true) can only clear an already empty map and assign the same flag, with no rental returns or baseline calls. If cleanup throws, both versions still have disposed=false and retry identically. Dispose(false) cannot be invoked by a subclass or finalizer. This changes no supported lifetime or resource ownership; the individual returns and clearing remain required.

The private disposed flag is read only by this cleanup guard, not by reads, writes or commits. The sealed internal stream is confined to UpdateStreamCore's using lifetime and never written after disposal. The original first cleanup still returns every rental, clears chunks and nulls rangeBytes before this assignment. Leaving the flag false merely allows a repeated cleanup to visit an empty map and null range; no resource can be returned twice and no baseline operation is added. A throwing cleanup reaches neither assignment in either version. This proof does not permit removing any actual rental return or metadata clearing.

SparseUpdateStream directly inherits System.IO.Stream. Stream.Dispose(bool) has an empty body on both supported runtimes (dotnet/runtime tags v8.0.0 and v10.0.0, src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Stream.cs). This base-qualified call cannot dispatch to a caller override or dispose the baseline. Removing it leaves all actual cleanup in the preceding derived body intact, including pooled returns, clearing, range reset and the disposed flag. Stream.Close still calls the derived Dispose(true) and suppresses finalization. This proof does not qualify removal of any derived cleanup operation.

This Dispose call targets only an exact private new MemoryStream(length) scratch wrapper, not the baseline, destination or a pooled page. CreateStagedRange exposes its backing byte array, which remains valid after MemoryStream disposal; the wrapper itself never escapes. After this call the wrapper is either overwritten by the next scratch stream or the iterator ends, without another read/write through that wrapper. MemoryStream owns no external handle and disposal neither returns a pooled buffer nor releases its backing array. Omitting this exact call changes no emitted bytes, stream I/O, buffer ownership or managed backing-array lifetime. The real pooled-page and contiguous-rental returns remain required.

TryGetPosition returns nullable Int64. If Position throws, the original catch returns null. Removing its body still catches that exception, and Stryker 5.0.0's EndingReturnEngine appends default(long?), also null. The caller therefore retains the same attempted-offset fallback and original commit failure. Tool implementation: https://github.com/stryker-mutator/stryker-net/blob/6e77a3451bac4793e9c839c3ff4055c1b30ca3af/src/Stryker.Core/Stryker.Core/Instrumentation/EndingReturnEngine.cs.

Only the empty-range case is newly admitted by rangeLength >= 0. The unchanged following bounds require address >= rangeStart and address < rangeStart + 0 simultaneously, which is impossible. The body never indexes the null buffer; the same false result and zero out value follow. Nonempty ranges behave identically.

TryStageInRange is called only while chunks is null. Before its first successful write rangeLength is zero and rangeBytes is null, so assignment and null-coalescing assignment rent the same buffer. Subsequent contiguous writes have positive rangeLength; promotion sets chunks non-null and this helper is never called again. Public updates own this internal staging stream in one using scope and never write after disposal. No supported operation reaches this line with an existing range buffer.

On every supported entry to this initial-range branch, rangeBytes is null and the preceding Rent requests at least source.Length. The ArrayPool contract guarantees at least that capacity. Its Length < source.Length branch therefore cannot execute; removing this unreachable return does not lose a rental. This does not qualify any return on the reachable contiguous-growth or promotion paths.

The initial-range branch rents at least source.Length when rangeBytes is null. This is the only supported pre-write state with zero rangeLength and no chunks: later writes are positive-length or use the chunk map. ArrayPool guarantees at least the requested capacity, so the smaller-buffer branch cannot execute and changing its unreachable clearArray argument has no effect.

PromoteRangeToChunks is called only after TryStageInRange returns false. That helper always handles rangeLength == 0 and returns true; only a gap outside an existing positive-length range returns false. Thus promotion always sees rangeLength > 0. Replacing > with >= leaves its copy, return and reset operations unchanged.

The bitmap's maximumWrittenExclusive is one past its last written byte. After the last emitted run offset equals that bound. Changing the outer loop to <= enters one extra iteration, but the unchanged inner loop short-circuits and the following equality immediately yields break. It emits no extra range and performs no bitmap lookup or I/O.

The unchanged outer loop starts this gap scan strictly below maximumWrittenExclusive. Every chunk is populated by a nonempty Write, which sets the bit at maximumWrittenExclusive - 1. The gap scan therefore encounters a written byte before reaching the exclusive bound. Changing only its < comparison to <= never evaluates IsWritten at the bound and yields identical runs.

Within the unchanged outer loop offset starts below maximumWrittenExclusive. The gap scan cannot pass the last written byte at maximumWrittenExclusive - 1, because Write sets that bit whenever it extends the maximum. Thus offset == maximumWrittenExclusive is false at this point on every reachable iteration; removing this defensive yield break changes no run or I/O.

Changing >= to > differs only when position equals the captured baselineLength. At that exact boundary Read computes available = Math.Min(buffer.Length, baselineLength - position) = 0, never enters its loop, adds zero to position and returns zero. Empty buffers also return zero. No baseline query or read occurs on either path.

CreateStagedRange is private and receives only the exact MemoryStream instances constructed with new MemoryStream(length) in GetStagedRanges. These expandable streams expose their managed backing arrays, including the non-null empty array. TryGetBuffer therefore returns true with a non-null Array on every reachable call. Replacing OR with AND leaves the defensive branch unentered.

CreateStagedRange receives only private new MemoryStream(length) instances from GetStagedRanges. Their backing arrays are publicly exposable and non-null, so the defensive hidden-buffer throw is unreachable. No caller-owned stream or subclass reaches this helper.

The hidden-buffer diagnostic belongs to an unreachable branch: GetStagedRanges constructs every input with new MemoryStream(length), which exposes its non-null backing array. Changing only that defensive message cannot affect an emitted StagedRange or a caller-visible failure.

The input is an owned, expandable MemoryStream created in GetStagedRanges, never a caller subclass. Its length is bounded by its single managed array and Int32 capacity; a write beyond that supported capacity fails before CreateStagedRange. Converting its successfully constructed Length to int cannot overflow.

The initial rangeStart sentinel is never emitted. On the first written run rangeBytes is null, so the branch assigns rangeStart = start before creating the first stream. Every subsequent replacement also assigns the start before creating that stream; with no runs the final emission is skipped. Initializing the sentinel to +1 instead of -1 is unobservable.

The initial expectedAddress is ignored because rangeBytes is null and the first operand of the branch short-circuits. The first run assigns expectedAddress = start + length before any later comparison. With no runs it is never read. Changing only its initial sentinel has no effect.

Chunk keys are created only by WriteToChunks as nonnegative address / 1024. Write validates position + buffer.Length with checked arithmetic and rejects ends beyond baselineLength before staging; promotion copies an already validated range. Therefore key * 1024 is no greater than an actual staged address and fits Int64. Removing checked from this multiplication cannot change behavior.

Each written run's offset identifies bytes previously copied by WriteToChunks, whose chunk key and offset come from one nonnegative extent-validated address. The sum chunkStart + offset recovers a staged address strictly below a successfully checked write end, so it cannot exceed Int64.MaxValue. Removing checked preserves values and failures.

GetWrittenRuns returns only contiguous bytes marked by successful extent-validated writes. The exclusive end start + length is at most the greatest checked end of those writes, even when adjacent writes merge. Every write end is at most baselineLength and Int64.MaxValue. Removing checked from the recovered run end cannot overflow.

IsLineContinuation recognizes only backslash-LF and backslash-CRLF. Advancing two characters already matches LF. For CRLF it leaves the cursor on LF; the next SkipWhitespace iteration recognizes that character as whitespace and advances once, reaching the same position as the original three-character step. There is no callback or published intermediate position inside this loop, and neither path can read beyond the source. This proof does not apply to SkipRestOfLine, where a remaining LF ends the scan.

FlushHoisted receives a private parser destination list and an index saved before a struct, union or typedef appends its declarations. With no hoisted declarations, that index is still valid, InsertRange receives an empty list and Clear clears an already empty list. No destination enumerator is alive or exposed while parsing. The additional empty-list operations leave the same declaration order and failures; nonempty hoisted lists already enter the original branch.

When the linked token can be cancelled, the original already selects this clone. Otherwise AsyncStreamBuffer.Link implies both input tokens are non-cancellable. UpdateOptions is sealed and contains only ordinary immutable properties; cloning it while assigning the same non-cancellable token preserves every option. A null input produces the same documented defaults used by the original region setup and Update snapshot. Update snapshots its options before use in both versions, so the extra clone changes allocation only, not values, cancellation, aliasing or failures. This proof does not cover the analogous unsealed WriteOptions branch, whose caller-defined derived copy constructor could be observable.

The null-value branch already returned or threw, and IsInstanceOfType already returned the non-null value for any assignable target. System.Object accepts every remaining boxed value, so its later dedicated branch is unreachable. Removing that block cannot change a conversion.

ConvertCore reaches GetElementType only when the runtime target Type has IsArray true. All production targets originate from typeof(T) or a runtime array element type, not a user-defined Type wrapper. Runtime array types always have an element Type, so the fallback InvalidOperationException and its text are unreachable.
