ConvertNumeric is called only after IsNumericType accepts one of the twelve supported numeric types, or with a CLR enum underlying integral type. Float, double, decimal and BigInteger return in their own branches; the eight fixed-width integral targets also each return or throw. The final failure after those branches is unreachable for supported targets.

CStructReadException(message) delegates to the protected constructor with ReadFailed, message and its default null innerException. CStructReadException(message, null) delegates to that same constructor with the identical three values. Selecting the two-argument overload when the cause is null preserves every exception member and subsequent path attachment.

This multiplication is reached only when peeling a multidimensional field with a known nonnegative element size. Multidimensional dimensions have dependency-free fixed counts; LayoutCompilation.Model and CompileSyntheticRootField already checked the complete count and element-size product when constructing such a field. All production SelectArrayElement callers are the read/address and write path resolvers, which first reject indices outside the current dimension. A reachable peeled dimension therefore has a positive outer count, so its remaining byte extent cannot exceed its already validated parent's extent. A zero outer count cannot be indexed; variable-sized elements skip this multiplication entirely. Repeated peeling preserves the bound, and pointer-target views are scalar. Removing only this checked wrapper cannot change a supported result; the separate checked total-count calculations remain required, including for arrays of variable-sized records.

CollectShapeNames follows only promoted anonymous by-value composites. LayoutCompilation.Model rejects recursive by-value declarations before exposing the compiled model; pointer edges are not promoted composites. The active visiting set therefore never contains a valid child being entered. Its defensive cycle return is unreachable for compiled layouts.

PromotedFields contains only declarations matching Struct with an empty name. Without this continue, the subsequent ordinary-name branch still rejects name.Length equal to zero. Recursive collection already occurred and no empty name is added, so the final shape is identical.

CollectShapeNames visits a finite acyclic graph of promoted by-value composites and deduplicates output names in the separate seen set. Leaving a completed composite in visiting can only skip a later traversal of that identical composite; its entire reachable name sequence was already visited and every name is already in seen. Thus neither final names nor their first-occurrence order changes. The visiting set is private to one BuildShape call.

restoreOrigin is true only for ResolveAddressAsync and GetArrayLengthAsync. Their synchronous core operations restore their borrowed FixedBufferStream to its initial position zero in finally, so consumed is zero on every successful query. origin + consumed is therefore origin when this branch changes. All consuming operations pass false and already take the unchanged origin + consumed branch; failures follow the separate restoration catch.

The changed branch is only the zero-origin fast return. Shift copies each private DebugData record with Start plus zero and End plus zero, preserving every other record member. The returned value is unchanged. Neither the original private result nor its list has escaped, so the extra result/list/record copies cannot change observable reference relationships with caller-owned objects or any coordinates.

For origin zero, Shift preserves every DebugData member and the selected result value; only private result/list/record objects are copied instead of returned directly. For nonzero origin the same shift already occurs. No original debug-list identity escapes this private callback, so decoded values, diagnostic ranges and caller-visible object relationships are unchanged.

ResolveAddressCore always restores its input position in finally. Its buffered input starts at zero, so RunOverBuffer observes consumed equal to zero on every successful address query. The false restoreOrigin branch therefore assigns origin plus zero instead of origin; failure restoration is handled independently by ReadBufferedAsync.

GetDynamicArrayLengthCore always restores the buffered input position in finally, including terminated-string scans. The buffer starts at zero, so consumed is zero on every successful length query. Setting restoreOrigin false assigns origin plus zero, exactly the original origin assignment; failure restoration is unchanged.

When the linked token is cancellable the selected expression is unchanged. Otherwise both source tokens are non-cancellable: copying the sealed ReadOptions record with CancellationToken.None preserves every option, and a null options argument becomes the same default settings used by SnapshotReadOptions. The options record has no custom getters or copy side effects and its identity is not exposed by these private operation delegates. Only an extra temporary options allocation can differ.

The private constructor is called only by TryCreate, whose eight accepted canonical StorageType values are exactly the eight explicit ToStorageValue switch cases. StorageType is a get-only property initialized there. The default unknown-storage exception is therefore unreachable for every constructible descriptor; changing only its message cannot affect a conversion or failure.

This changes only the preliminary eligibility check for selected-path root materialization. Non-null non-member sources already take the same branch. The additional cases are null and member-source dictionaries: WriteDataBinding.Materialize returns those exact inputs immediately, before allocating a StructValue or invoking a mapper. IsMemberSource uses only interface type tests, so checking null has no callback. TryGetRootComposite examines the immutable root declaration and, for a compiled Struct or inline-struct typedef, reads its already-bound descriptor from the private symbol table; other roots return false. Neither extra lookup nor the early-return materialization changes caller data, state or failure behavior. The later path lookup and field writer therefore receive the same object (including null). This does not qualify removal of the distinct whole-composite null rejection in the write engine.

WritePrimitiveValue has three callers. WriteSingleFieldValue first handles pointers, bitfields, enums and composites, then rejects HasCodec=false before calling it. WriteFixedCharArray handles bounded and wide text separately; its remaining per-character caller has the compiled built-in char codec. The compiled engine calls it only for a LEB128 or variable-size custom value in update staging, from a program whose compiler refused any field without a codec writer. BuildCodecTable fills every canonical id with a non-null writer and appends a non-null adapter delegate for every validated custom registration. Thus both callers supply an existing writer. A custom writer may throw, but cannot make its registered delegate null. The separate reachable no-handler error for a void alias is unaffected.

PrepareWrite rejects blank paths before ParsePath. CStructPathResolver.ParseUncached starts segmentCount at one and either throws or returns an array of that positive length. Both successful TryCreateSyntheticRoot branches return exactly one segment; false branches cannot replace the parsed result. The two private caches only store these successful results, and no caller changes their length. Therefore ParsePath cannot return an empty segment list to this writer. Removing only the second, unreachable empty-list throw changes neither accepted paths nor the earlier empty-path diagnostic.

PrepareWrite rejects blank paths before ParsePath. The ordinary path parser returns an array with at least one segment or throws; successful synthetic roots contain exactly one segment. Their private caches retain only these nonempty results. Thus the second empty-list guard cannot be reached, and changing only its diagnostic string has no observable effect. The earlier reachable empty-path exception remains unchanged.

For supported one-byte encoding units (ASCII/UTF-8 NUL or newline terminators), the encoded terminator has one byte and the first encoding boundary is offset zero. Both production callers calculate alignmentOffset modulo unitSize, which is zero when unitSize is one. Removing this vectorized IndexOf fast path therefore falls through to a loop comparing that same byte at every index from zero, returning the same first match or minus one. Two-byte encodings already use the loop and are unchanged. This is an optimization-only change for supported terminator inputs, not a claim about malformed helper arguments.

ReadUInt48 starts with zero and places each of six bytes at a distinct multiple-of-eight shift, in either byte order. The new byte's bit positions never overlap accumulated bits, so OR and XOR produce identical 48-bit values.

The preceding exact case 8 already returns ReadUInt64 for every eight-byte input. This fallback only receives widths 3, 5, 6 and 7; changing its upper bound from <= 8 to < 8 cannot change any selected case or result.

The generic ReadUnsigned loop starts with zero and assigns each source byte a distinct eight-bit position within at most 64 bits. The new byte cannot overlap previously accumulated bits, so OR and XOR yield the same value for both byte orders.

The preceding exact case 8 already writes all eight-byte destinations and breaks. The generic fallback only receives widths 3, 5, 6 and 7, so changing its upper bound to < 8 does not change dispatch or output.
WriteUnsigned's value is ulong. Both >> and >>> shift this unsigned operand with zero fill and the same masked shift count, producing identical destination bytes.
WriteULeb128's value is ulong. Compound >>= and >>>= both use zero-fill shifts for this unsigned operand, so every subsequent value, continuation bit and output byte is identical.

Decimal multiplication and conversion from double to decimal throw OverflowException on an unrepresentable result regardless of checked context. Removing this checked expression does not turn either decimal operation into wrapping arithmetic, and exact-grid validation still receives the same scaled decimal or the same exception.
ExtractBits receives unit as ulong. Both right-shift operators zero-fill the same unsigned bits with the same shift-count masking before the unchanged bit mask is applied.
WriteUInt24Unchecked's value is uint, so >> and >>> both zero-fill before conversion to the middle output byte. The same eight low bits are written.
WriteUInt24Unchecked's value is uint, so >> and >>> both zero-fill before conversion to the high output byte. The byte-order-dependent destination index and written byte are unchanged.
WriteUInt48Unchecked's value is ulong. Both shift operators zero-fill this unsigned operand, preserving all six extracted bytes for either byte order.

The changed branch applies only to an empty baseline. Enumerating a dictionary with Count zero contributes zero entries, so the fallback computes storage.Count + 0, exactly the fast branch's count. Nonempty baselines already take this fallback. Enumeration overhead is not a different dictionary result; a custom dictionary whose Count disagrees with its entries violates the input contract.

Every enum starts resolution with a new local visiting set, and each scalar alias has exactly one recursive successor. This removal only skips cleanup while returning or unwinding that single chain: no sibling is visited and no caller observes or reuses the set. Cycle detection before recursion remains intact; both successful results and circular-alias failures are unchanged.

The extra branch runs only when evaluated equals highestBitSeen. Its sole statement assigns evaluated to highestBitSeen, leaving the exact BigInteger value unchanged. Subsequent implicit flag values and all validation therefore remain identical.

Only the zero case changes which expression is evaluated. BigInteger.Zero.GetBitLength() is zero, and shifting BigInteger.One by zero produces BigInteger.One, exactly the omitted branch's result. The nonzero case is unchanged, so every next implicit flag value is identical.

Both codec callers support the documented widths 32 and 64. shift starts at zero and advances by seven, so it cannot equal either width. The changed equality boundary is unreachable; unsupported widths or reusing the decoder after completion/failure are not claimed equivalent inputs.

For supported widths 32 and 64, the final permitted group begins at shift 28 or 63. The remaining-width guard then rejects any continuation bit before shift can advance beyond the width; otherwise Push returns true and both callers stop. Therefore this defensive throw is never reached by either codec caller, including malformed encodings, and removing it changes no supported operation.

remaining is width minus a multiple of seven. The supported widths 32 and 64 have remainders four and one modulo seven, so remaining can never equal seven. Both conditions validate exactly the same final group.

Before each Push, accumulated payload bits are strictly below shift. Each new seven-bit payload starts at shift and has no set bit in common with the accumulated value, including truncation of the final 64-bit group. OR and XOR therefore produce identical bits. Sign extension only occurs on completion, after which both callers stop using the decoder.

shift starts at zero and only advances by seven. Thus shift + 7 is a multiple of seven and never 64 during a supported decoding operation. The changed equality boundary cannot affect whether sign extension runs.

The preceding payload accumulation fills bits strictly below shift + 7, and this branch requires shift + 7 < 64. The extension mask sets only the higher bits, which are still zero. Its OR and XOR with the accumulated payload therefore yield exactly the same signed representation.

For a supported SetLength request, value and the original Stream.Length are both nonnegative Int64 byte lengths. Their difference is between -Int64.MaxValue and Int64.MaxValue, so this subtraction cannot overflow. The same Math.Max, budget check and underlying SetLength run. Negative requested lengths or a stream reporting a negative Length violate the stream operation's input contract and are not equivalent-input claims.

For supported streams and block lengths, Position, length and initialLength are nonnegative. The retained inner checked addition either throws as before or produces a nonnegative Int64 write end. Subtracting a nonnegative Int64 initial length from that end cannot exceed either signed bound, so removing only the outer subtraction check changes no result or overflow handling.

Supported write counts and stream positions are nonnegative. The preceding checked Position + count either throws before this line or yields a nonnegative Int64 writeEnd; initialLength is also nonnegative. Their difference therefore lies within the signed Int64 range. The separate cumulative-traffic and write-end addition checks remain unchanged.

Removing the inner checked wrapper leaves the addition textually inside the outer checked expression around addition minus initialLength. C# checked context covers both integral operators in that expression, so overflow from Position + length still reaches the same catch and returns false. The existing extreme-position preflight regression exercises this boundary.

Only the catch body is removed; the exception remains caught. Stryker.NET 5.0.0 injects an ending return default(long?) for this non-void method whose last statement is a try/catch. Thus a failed Position getter still returns null, while a successful getter still returns its value. Verified against EndingReturnEngine.InjectReturn and BaseFunctionOrchestrator.InjectMutations at the package's repository commit 6e77a3451bac4793e9c839c3ff4055c1b30ca3af; this proof depends on the pinned tool instrumentation, not on treating an uncompilable source edit as detected.

PlaceSeparator ends the SysV run. Every caller (static layout, runtime cursor and generated cursor) immediately uses RunEnd, which independently clamps the rounded bit position to cellEnd. Write C = cellEnd >= 0 and A = the unchanged aligned bit position. For C < 2^60, C*8 fits: if A exceeds C*8 both variants select A; otherwise the original rounds to C and the variant rounds to at most C, then RunEnd restores C. For C >= 2^60, any unchecked Int64 result of (bitPosition + 7)/8 is strictly less than C, so both RunEnd values equal C even if intermediate multiplication wraps. CheckForOverflowUnderflow is false and these expressions are not checked. The next Place or separator initializes bitPosition from the identical current byte boundary because runActive is false; Close resets it. No caller observes the differing intermediate bitPosition.

For MSVC, RunEnd is unitStart + unitSize. All three owners (PlaceCompiledFields, CompositeFieldPlacementCursor and generated CompositeCursor) set current to RunEnd after every placed bitfield or separator. Ordinary fields close the run before changing current. Thus when a run is active both alternatives are equal; when inactive the original already selects current.

The separator immediately sets runActive true, unitStart to next and unitSize zero, overwriting Close's relevant placement changes. The remaining difference is stale BitsUsed and cellEnd: cellEnd is never used in MSVC placement, and the next nonzero field must start a new unit because its positive declared size differs from zero, resetting BitsUsed before use. Repeated separators and Close also ignore or reset that stale state.

All placement owners update current to the MSVC RunEnd (unitStart + unitSize) after each bitfield or separator and close the run before an ordinary field changes current. Opening the next unit therefore selects the same byte position with either active-run alternative. For an inactive run both versions already use current.

After an MSVC separator, unitSize is zero and all three owners assign current = RunEnd = unitStart. No production consumer reads InRun. The next positive-size field starts a new unit with either flag value, using identical current/unitStart and resetting BitsUsed; another separator also chooses equal positions, and an ordinary field closes the run. Thus the changed intermediate flag affects neither placement nor storage.

The immediately preceding unconditional Close call already sets unitSize to zero. The intervening assignments change only runActive and unitStart. Removing this second unitSize = 0 assignment therefore leaves exactly the same complete placement state.

Only null bypasses this block originally. Without it, null does not match Pointer and reaches Convert.ToInt64(object), whose null result is also zero. No conversion callback or failure is introduced; every non-null value follows the identical path.

The preceding pattern requires the promoted field's name length to be zero. After the recursive collection returns, the next guard tests that same immutable name length and continues. Removing the first continue therefore reaches an identical continue without adding a name or changing recursion.

Only count zero newly reaches budget arithmetic. bytesRead starts at zero and only accepted charges update it, so it never exceeds the nonnegative fixed limit. Adding zero cannot overflow or fail the limit check and reassigns the same value; position is unchanged. Negative counts still return early.

This sizing cursor always starts at zero; it never starts at a caller's stream address. Its immutable Fields array has at most Int32.MaxValue entries. Each validated alignment adds at most Int32.MaxValue - 1 padding bytes, and each successfully computed field storage is a nonnegative Int32; bitfield placement advances by at most its alignment padding plus an at-most-eight-byte unit. With M = Int32.MaxValue, even M ordinary fields therefore end at or below M * (2*M - 1) = 9223372026117357571, below Int64.MaxValue. This particular Int64 addition cannot overflow. Removing its checked wrapper preserves nested sizing failures and the final checked Int32 conversion. This proof does not cover Int32 array-count or storage multiplication, nor cursors based at caller-supplied stream positions.

An empty compiled composite has no conditional fields and no storage. The ordinary struct cursor starts at zero and its empty traversal finishes at zero; an empty union also has largest extent zero. Validated positive alignment leaves zero unchanged. Removing the early empty-fields return therefore still returns zero without evaluating any field expression.

After the scalar return and Flexible/ToEnd/Terminated rejection, only Fixed and Runtime shapes remain. Every production shape constructor in LayoutCompilation.Model assigns their parsed dimension expression, and PeelOuterDimension copies the next validated fixed dimension. Their CountExpression cannot be null; changing this defensive message affects no compiled layout.

All Fixed and Runtime dimensions are created from parsed non-null expressions by LayoutCompilation.Model. Scalar shapes return before this loop and data-sized shapes throw before it. Peeling preserves those expressions. Thus the per-dimension null-expression fallback cannot be reached by a compiled layout; changing only its text has no effect.

Only composites without direct conditions gain a selection object. Their constructor leaves every field's ConditionalBranches empty, so IsActive returns true without evaluating anything. The original null selection also skips no field. The same placement and size arithmetic runs; only an unused selection allocation is added.

Every scalar shape produced by the compiler uses CompiledArrayShape.Scalar with an empty Dimensions array. Without the fast return it bypasses the flexible-kind check, starts total at 1, executes zero loop iterations and returns 1. Other array kinds already bypass this block.

ResolveFieldTypeReference is called only by CompileComposite, after BuildCompiledLayout has resolved every typedef into namedTypes. ResolveCompiledTypeReference therefore returns a cached type, resolves a pointer-sized primitive spelling, or throws its Unknown field type exception with the default negative SourceOffset. Alias-cycle and alias-kind failures occur in the earlier typedef pass and cannot reach this catch filter. Both filter operands are true for its only reachable exception, so OR catches exactly the same failure as AND and preserves the field-specific diagnostic.

All typedefs have been resolved before the sole CompileComposite caller reaches this helper. The called type resolver can then fail only with its Unknown field type exception, constructed without a source offset; it has the negative default, never zero. The original prefix test is unchanged. Replacing < 0 with <= 0 therefore catches the same exceptions; the handler still attaches the actual field-type source offset afterwards.

The empty prefix makes StartsWith true, but the only exception that can reach this filter already starts with Unknown field type. BuildCompiledLayout resolves every typedef before compiling composite fields, so circular or mismatched typedef failures happen before the sole caller. Cached known types and pointer-sized primitive spellings return without throwing. No additional exception is intercepted; the same unknown-type handler retains the field name, owner, hint and source position.

spelling is the parsed field type name. The parser constructs it from a nonempty first identifier and inserts spaces only between subsequent type-name words; typedef normalization substitutes another parsed identifier spelling. It never starts with a space. IndexOf therefore returns -1 or a positive index, not zero, so >= 0 and > 0 take the same branch and produce the same missing-semicolon hint. Custom codec names are also validated as identifiers and cannot introduce a leading space.

The surrounding branch requires space > 0, and secondSpace is IndexOf starting at space + 1. Its result is therefore either -1 or at least 2, never zero. The original > 0 and mutated >= 0 predicates select the same substring for every reached input.

A successful forward seek starts Reserve at the old length and reserves requested position minus that length, leaving position exactly equal to the requested position. Without the return, the following assignment writes that same value. A failing Reserve still throws before either path can continue.

Grow is called only when required exceeds the old destination length. Math.Max still makes the requested rental at least required after this mutation; copying the written prefix, clearing the remaining capacity and replacing/returning buffers are unchanged. Future reservations remain capacity-checked. Only the private spare-capacity policy and resulting allocation frequency change, not encoded bytes, positions, limits or buffer ownership.

The only newly entered case is position equal to length. Its body only assigns length = position, leaving the same integer state. Both versions return the same reserved span and perform identical capacity and budget checks.

When the linked token can cancel, this already takes the clone branch. Otherwise neither input token can cancel: cloning the sealed ReadOptions preserves every setting and assigns the same non-cancellable token; null denotes the same default settings as new ReadOptions. The documented read settings are unchanged. The extra descriptor allocation and descriptor reference identity are not record-reading results.

This string names an expression-tree temporary only for debugging. The block declaration, TryGetValue output and selected result all use the same ParameterExpression instance, so changing its diagnostic label cannot change variable binding, returned union members or missing-member behavior. The private temporary's label is not part of the dynamic member contract.

Removing the early null return makes NormalizeRootData call TryGetMemberValue with null. That helper returns false and assigns a null out value before reading members. The conditional therefore returns the same original null data. No mapper or member lookup is invoked on either path, and null root pointers remain supported.

mutants.replacement: data is IDictionary<string, object?> && data is IDictionary<string, object>
mutants.reason: Nullable reference annotations do not create different runtime generic types: IDictionary<string, object?> and IDictionary<string, object> have identical CLR identity. Their two is-tests always agree for every object, including null; replacing OR with AND therefore produces the same Boolean result.

MaterializeElement receives non-null values only. For member sources, Materialize returns the same object immediately. For sealed UnionValue, which cannot implement the constrained mapping interface, TryWrite cannot find a registered mapper and Materialize returns the same object. All other values already use Materialize. Only an unused temporary StructValue allocation can differ; returned identity, nested mapping and caller data are unchanged.

IsMemberSource and UnionValue are disjoint: sealed UnionValue implements IReadOnlyDictionary, not IDictionary. Replacing OR with AND sends these two cases through Materialize, which returns member sources immediately and returns the unregistered sealed UnionValue unchanged. Other values already take that path. The extra temporary allocation for UnionValue does not change returned identity or mapping behavior.

Nullable reference annotations do not produce distinct CLR types. IDictionary<string, object?> and IDictionary<string, object> match exactly the same objects. Removing the first branch falls through to the second identical TryGetValue assignment and return; found, value and dictionary side effects are unchanged.

The earlier IDictionary<string, object?> branch matches exactly the same CLR type as IDictionary<string, object> and always returns. This second branch is unreachable; removing it cannot affect any lookup, output or dictionary side effect.

The following conditional tests the same CLR dictionary type, because nullable reference annotations erase at runtime, and returns the same Keys property. Removing the first branch neither changes the returned enumerable nor adds a Keys evaluation.

EncodeFixedPoint validates signedness and range before this branch. Width 16 takes the unchanged first branch. For the 32-bit path, unchecked int and uint casts retain the identical low 32 bits; BinaryPrimitiveIO and Codec signed/unsigned writers both emit those exact four bits-per-byte groups in the requested endian order using the same stream.Write call. Flipping signed only selects an equivalent bit writer, without changing validation, byte count or I/O behavior.

Removing the cache-hit return reparses the identical immutable string with the same deterministic ParseUncached routine. Production consumers use only names and index values, never segment-array identity, and do not mutate the cached arrays. Cache hits can only exist for previously valid strings; null and invalid input follow the unchanged validation path. Only parsing/allocation work differs.

The caller already recognized an enum/flag typedef. SkipKeyword does not compare the supplied spelling; it advances by keyword.Length and skips trivia. Both flag and enum are four characters, so always supplying flag moves the same cursor and encounters the same trivia/errors. The separately computed isFlag boolean is unchanged and still controls the resulting enum/flag declaration. No allocation, source offset, parsed member, type identity or runtime behavior changes.

SkipKeyword consumes a keyword already recognized by its caller and uses only the argument's length before SkipTrivia. Enum and flag both have length four; always supplying enum advances identically for either spelling. The local isFlag value is not mutated and is still passed to enum construction, so flag identity and values remain intact. All subsequent parsing, source offsets, failures and allocations are unchanged.

Removing the initial ParseEnumMember call does not omit the first member: the following loop parses it instead. The preceding IsIdentifierPart guard ensures the cursor is on a letter, digit or underscore, so the loop's first TryToken(',') fails without advancing or skipping trivia, and its identifier-part check succeeds. It then invokes the same ParseEnumMember and adds the same value. From that point both versions execute the same loop with the same cursor and list. Empty bodies return before this statement. No token, source offset, exception, allocation or ordering changes; only two side-effect-free token checks move ahead of the first parse.

For names beginning with a letter or underscore, ExpectIdentifier and the numeric-name fallback consume the same maximal IsIdentifierPart run, construct the same Identifier string and SourceOffset, and call SkipTrivia once. TryParseIdentifier's do/while and the fallback's while both consume the guaranteed first identifier character and stop at the same delimiter. Their Substring/range expressions create the same single string value, and neither accepts stars or type markers. Removing this fast-path body therefore sends ordinary names through an equivalent parser; digit-leading and invalid names already take the unchanged fallback.

For an empty dimensions list, the newly entered foreach has no iterations and BuildArrayCount immediately returns Field.NoArray, exactly the original shape value. Nonempty lists already enter the original branch. The private List is operation-owned, so the changed count comparison preserves the produced typedef, validation failures and array-shape identity.

TryRecognizeBinaryOperator's only caller is TryBinaryOperator, called from ParseBinary. ParseBinary returns through ParseUnary before reaching TryBinaryOperator at UnaryLevel. Every recognized operator has positive length; the unrecognized fallback alone has length zero and operatorLevel UnaryLevel. Thus the fallback's level comparison is false for every caller, even if length >= 0 becomes true; the recognized cases remain unchanged.

When the star is missing, TryStartFunctionPointer restores the cursor to its opening parenthesis and returns false. The sole caller then finds no array, bit-width, placement or comma suffix at that parenthesis and fails ExpectToken for a semicolon there; temporary field construction performs no validation. Returning true instead takes the caller directly to the same ExpectToken at the identical cursor. Both paths throw the same syntax error before returning any field or changing parser-visible state.

Failed function-signature recognition restores the cursor to the original opening parenthesis and clears name. The sole caller accepts a true result only by first requiring a semicolon at that cursor, which fails. The original false path cannot consume the parenthesis as an array, bit-width, placement or comma suffix and reaches the same semicolon check after non-validating temporary field construction. Thus the same error and location are produced; no opaque pointer field escapes either path.

BuildTypeIdentifier is private and has one call site in ParseFieldDeclaration. That caller rejects words.Count == 0 before parsing suffixes, and no subsequent operation changes the local words list before this call. The source-offset conditional therefore always selects words[0].SourceOffset; forcing its true arm is equivalent.

BuildTypeIdentifier is private and has one call site in ParseFieldDeclaration. That caller rejects an empty words list, and the list is not changed between the guard and this call. Both words.Count > 0 and words.Count >= 0 are true for every reachable invocation, preserving the first word's source offset.

BuildTypeIdentifier's sole private caller rejects an empty words list before invoking it. The fallback -1 source offset is therefore unreachable; changing only that fallback to +1 cannot change a returned identifier or diagnostic.

ParseDefine already called SkipInlineTrivia before inspecting the value kind. The empty, macro and quoted branches return; the integer-expression branch reaches this second call without changing the cursor. The earlier call stopped on the same non-trivia character, so repeating it consumes nothing and cannot introduce a new failure. Removing only the second call leaves expression parsing and text fallback unchanged.

The local value is initialized to null immediately before this try. Its only assignment evaluates ParseExpr fully before storing the result. If ParseExpr throws, that assignment does not occur and value is still null; SkipInlineTrivia cannot assign it either. The catch still catches the same CStructLayoutException when its body is empty. Both versions then reset to valueStart and read the identical text fallback.

This helper is called only after ParseExpr returned successfully. Every successful expression leaf or closing delimiter consumes trailing trivia, and unary/binary/conditional wrappers preserve that final cursor. Thus end is EOF or points to a non-trivia character, never a physical line ending or a valid continuation. Allowing index equal to end examines at most that extra non-line-ending character; the separate source-length guard prevents an EOF read. It cannot change the detected line-break result or parser state.

LineBreakBetween is called only by ParseDefine with end equal to the current parser position, after the preceding AtEnd condition in the same OR expression was false. Therefore end < source.Length. The loop's unchanged index < end condition is evaluated first and guarantees index < source.Length whenever this second bound is reached. Both < and <= source.Length are true for every such index, including empty ranges where neither is evaluated. No additional character, line break or continuation is examined.

This SkipInactiveBranch call follows popping the innermost conditional at #endif. Every conditional actually pushed by ParsePreprocessorLine has active ancestors: an inactive branch is scanned by SkipInactiveBranch, which counts nested directives locally without pushing them and returns only at that branch's own #else/#endif. After the pop, the stack is therefore empty or its new innermost entry is active. SkipInactiveBranch immediately returns for both states, without touching the cursor or diagnostics. Unmatched #endif throws before the pop/call. Removing this specific no-op call cannot expose skipped content or alter malformed-input handling.

ReadRestOfLine has only two callers. The macro caller starts at its required opening parenthesis, which is appended before any continuation. The text fallback starts at valueStart after SkipInlineTrivia has consumed every leading whitespace/comment/valid continuation; empty or line-ended bodies already returned, so its first character is appended normally. The builder is never cleared. Consequently every later continuation reaches this guard with Length > 0, and changing it to >= 0 neither accesses an empty builder nor changes separator insertion. Invalid backslashes are appended as ordinary characters and preserve the same invariant.

The include terminator search starts at position + 1 after consuming the #include keyword and recognizing its opening delimiter. Any found index is therefore strictly positive; IndexOf reports -1 when no terminator exists. A result of zero is impossible, so changing end < 0 to end <= 0 preserves every successful include and missing-delimiter failure.

NormalizeStructExpressions evaluates bit widths against staticLayoutVariables and rebuilds every ordinary Field through its integer-width constructor before capture marking. BitSizeExpression is consequently a Literal or NoneExpr, both immediate no-ops in AddReferences. Inline Struct declarations also carry no bit-width expression. Removing this call cannot omit a runtime dependency or change bit-width validation, placement or capture.

DeclaredValues retains enum source expressions, but EvaluateEnumDeclaration has already validated and frozen the members and CreateQualifiedMemberDefinitions has published literal Enum.Member definitions. Runtime enum reads/writes use the compiled integer table, not these source expressions. A data field whose name appears only in an enum initializer cannot influence the enum. Other runtime references and define dependencies are collected independently. Omitting this static-only capture source leaves enum validation, values, sizes, names and runtime expressions unchanged.

The executable calls accepted in layout dimensions are sizeof and offsetof, folded during compilation. Their callee identifiers name operators, not input variables. Unsupported expression calls fail compilation before a usable layout is returned. A field literally named sizeof or offsetof can still be captured if used as an ordinary identifier elsewhere, because that separate use is collected. Omitting the call target from this capture-only traversal does not remove call validation, folding or any runtime dependency.

Accepted sizeof/offsetof arguments are validated type/member names and are folded to a literal before a dimension executes. They do not refer to input-field values; unsupported call forms fail during compilation. Array arithmetic outside the call is still walked normally, and any ordinary runtime use of the same spelling is collected separately. Removing only argument capture bookkeeping preserves call validation, type/member lookup, folded sizes and all data-dependent expressions.

mutants.replacement: expression is null || ReferenceEquals(expression, NoneExpr.Instance) && expression is Literal
mutants.reason: This only sends NoneExpr and Literal leaves through the traversal instead of the fast return. Neither matches any traversal switch arm, so each is pushed and popped without adding a reference. The collected identifier set is identical; only temporary stack allocation/work can differ.

This sends null and NoneExpr through the traversal; Literal still returns early. Stack.Push accepts null and the switch has no null or NoneExpr arm, so traversal adds no identifiers and finishes with the same empty pending stack. No expression dependency changes.

Removing this leaf fast return only traverses null, NoneExpr and Literal. None matches an identifier or child-bearing expression arm; the stack accepts the item, pops it and is empty again. The referenced set and all later capture decisions remain unchanged.

Every completed traversal drains pending to zero; early-return paths never add to it, and it is private to this collection pass. Replacing the reusable empty stack with another empty stack therefore visits the same expressions and collects the same identifiers, at an extra allocation cost only.

The two nonnegative depths count pointer stars in the field declarator and its finite typedef chain. Cyclic aliases have already been rejected, so the chain cannot reuse a declaration's stars. Their sum is bounded by the number of characters in the single validated layout string, whose Length is an Int32; the source also contains the required non-star declaration characters. Built-in/custom symbols add no pointer stars. This sum cannot overflow for a layout accepted through the string-based compiler, even with an increased source-length option.

The extra path handles nonempty dimensions without calls. FoldCalls returns leaves unchanged and rebuilds unary/binary/conditional nodes with identical operators and children; there are no calls to resolve. Such dimensions were already compiled and validated by NormalizeStructExpressions. The unsized sentinel takes the unchanged direct arm and remains the exact sentinel. Empty scalar dimensions still skip the block. Equivalent expression objects/cache work may be added, but array kind, counts, dependencies, validation and runtime results are unchanged.

The folded dimension is subsequently passed to CompileArrayShape, whose single- and multidimensional paths call GetDependencies and hence the same cached GetProgram before evaluation or returning the compiled model. Only an unsized sentinel bypasses that compilation, and the unchanged outer guard already skips it. Eager compilation here therefore duplicates required construction-time compilation later; removing it changes no accepted expression, limit, diagnostic or runtime count.

The preceding guard admits only sizeof and offsetof calls. ParsePostfix parses every argument of these built-ins through ParseTypeArgument, which returns an Identifier or rejects the syntax; arithmetic arguments cannot reach FoldCalls. The unchanged arity check short-circuits for zero or otherwise incorrect argument counts. For the remaining one or two Identifier arguments, the non-Identifier predicate is false for every element, so both Any and All are false. Folding therefore accepts the same parsed calls and retains the same arity/type diagnostics.

Only an empty array-dimension list changes the left predicate. The unchanged right operand is Any(ContainsCall), which returns false without invoking the predicate for that empty list. The combined condition remains false and no folding or compilation occurs; nonempty lists follow the identical path.

A valid typedef chain has distinct declarations and reaches a non-alias or the unchanged pointer stop within the declaration count. An extra zero-counter iteration cannot extend such a chain. Cyclic aliases still fail the compiled type resolver before any layout is returned; the extra iteration neither repairs a cycle nor changes its declarations. Pointer-alias validation uses the same bounded walk.

The complete branch has already stored rewritten[current], and its child expressions were completed before that frame. Falling through only pushes current and those children again. Each extra frame immediately hits the unchanged rewritten.ContainsKey guard and skips; no mapping, constant substitution or expression is rewritten a second time. This proof depends on retaining that earlier guard and does not qualify removing it.

The preceding switch arm still handles every inline-composite typedef. The newly matched case is an ordinary alias with zero array dimensions. NormalizeTypedefArray preserves its Name, Type and TypeKeywordHint, and EvaluateTypedefShape performs zero iterations and returns an empty shape. All alias-shape consumers use Count/enumeration, not empty-list reference identity; no field array sentinel is replaced. The internal parsed alias has no caller-held identity through CStruct's string construction. Only an equivalent alias object and empty array are allocated.

The very next operation evaluates the same dimension with LayoutExpressionEvaluator. ExpressionEvaluator.Evaluate obtains the same cached GetProgram before executing it; removing this eager Compile only defers that identical compilation to the immediate evaluation. Compilation failures are CStructLayoutException and pass through LayoutExpressionEvaluator unchanged. Values, negative-count checks, evaluation diagnostics and work/depth limits remain enforced at construction.

For a non-null shape both versions return the same tuple values. For a null shape the mutant allocates an Identifier and returns a tuple whose second item is null. The field-normalization caller uses the typed tuple pattern 'is (Identifier elementType, IReadOnlyList<Expr> typedefShape)', which rejects that null second item just as it rejects the original nullable null result, leaving the original type and dimensions unchanged. The pointer-alias validation caller discards either return value and relies only on exceptions. No tuple escapes these private calls.

RejectNonIntegerConstants is the immediate next call, and its first operation is expressionEvaluator.GetDependencies(dimension). That method obtains the same GetProgram used by Compile, so compilation and all syntax-tree limits still run before constant validation or evaluation, with no intervening state change. The same cached program, dependencies and exceptions result. This removes only a redundant cache warm-up, not dimension validation.

Only the empty branch list changes arms. Selecting and materializing an empty list produces another empty branch array without invoking the projection, so NormalizeConditionalGroup is not called and a null normalizedGroups value is never accessed. All consumers inspect branch contents/counts, not array reference identity. Nonempty lists execute the identical projection in both versions. No condition, selector, arm or field visibility changes.

This changes only the availability subexpression of the outer preflight; its byte-budget condition remains required. A newly admitted case still calls TryReadSpan, which repeats the original memoryBacked and remaining-length checks before touching bytes or accounting. It returns false with a default span on every unavailable/non-memory case. Cases admitted by the original outer check remain admitted, with identical reads and budget charges.

TryReadSpan repeats the original subtraction-based availability check. If a nonnegative requested count is available, the memoryBacked conjunct has already excluded a stream-mode core, and every memory core holds an Int32-sized buffer (a FixedBufferStream region, an exposed MemoryStream array, the span, array or memory the engine pins, or a buffered form's pooled copy) with its position at most the whole input's length (below 2^48 bytes for a partly buffered input), so buffer length + position cannot overflow Int64 and is at least buffer length - position. Thus every originally successful preflight still reaches the same read. Extra candidates are rejected by the unchanged inner check without consuming or charging bytes.

This branch runs only when count fits the remaining budget. The mutation additionally admits count == 0, which adds 0 to bytesRead and leaves the total, the remaining budget and every later charge unchanged. Negative counts are still excluded, so no charge can be given back through this path.

The mutation workflow runs on net10.0, whose Int128 division and remainder throw DivideByZeroException, with the same default message, for every dividend when the divisor is zero. Without this statement Divide and Modulo still reject a zero divisor through the runtime operator, before any result is used, so no value, failure type, message or evaluation order changes on net10.0. The statement exists for net8.0, whose 128-bit division throws IndexOutOfRangeException or ArgumentOutOfRangeException for dividends of 64 bits or more; ExpressionArithmeticBoundaryTests.ZeroDivisor_FailsAsDivisionByZeroForEveryDividend kills the mutant there.

For non-null UpdateOptions the specialized branch and the fallback both evaluate a record with-expression with no member changes on the same input. Record cloning uses the runtime type, so the fallback still returns a fresh UpdateOptions preserving its derived settings as well as every base setting. Null and ordinary WriteOptions do not take the removed branch. Snapshot identity and values are unchanged.

Removing Runtime and ToEnd from the resolve-first kinds changes only who takes those root counts first: the path resolver (Count, DynamicArrayExtent.CountToEnd) or the root program (EvaluateCount, CountToEnd). Both evaluate the same count expression or the same arithmetic count from the input length, fail with the same ReadFailures text (negative count, element limit, partial element) at offset 0, read and charge no byte, and note no member (the root program does not note members). A terminated root is never resolved first (the read scans it once, RootCountResolutionTests), and a multidimensional one still checks its outermost count first (the Dimensions test is unchanged).

Dimensions.Length >= 1 adds one-dimensional fixed roots to the resolve-first kinds (a scalar root has no dimensions). The resolver checks such a count exactly as the root program checks it (CheckFixedCount before placement): the same ReadFailures.ArrayLengthLimit text at offset 0, with nothing read or charged and no member noted, so the added resolution changes no outcome.

size >= 0 adds arrays of zero-size elements, whose unit becomes 0 instead of the element composite's alignment or 1. Restart(0) keeps the previous guarantee (gcd(g, 0) = g, and 1 when g is 0). An array of zero-size elements always occupies 0 bytes, so the position is unchanged and the previous guarantee still holds: every placement it produces is correct, and the executor aligns and seeks to the same offsets.

The mutation also returns a composite member's alignment in a packed layout. A packed layout never consults the placement guarantee: Placement.Place and TryFinish return before they read the anchor when the layout is not aligned, so the unit changes no step and no offset.

Merge reaches this line only with different states. The common guarantee is 0 only when both guarantees are 0, which requires anchor 0 and delta 0 in both states: equal states, already returned above. common is therefore at least 1, and the replaced conditional is never true.

With alignment 1 the original returns false at once; the mutation continues: anchor % 1 is 0, AlignUp(delta, 1) is delta, the padding is 0 and the method returns false without a step, leaving delta unchanged. Alignments below 1 do not occur (a member's alignment is at least 1).
The padding before an aligned member is less than its alignment, a small power of two, so the conversion to int cannot overflow and the checked context never throws.

delta grows only by the storage sizes of members placed after one anchor, each an int, and is reset at every dynamic member; a composite's total size is bounded by the layout compilation (FixedSize is an int), so the sum stays far below the long range and the checked context never throws.

Restart's unit is at least 1 (MemberExtents.ExtentUnit returns an element size above 0, an alignment of at least 1, or 1), so gcd(guarantee, unit) is at least 1 and the replaced conditional is never true.

With a composite alignment of 1 the original returns true with padding 0; the mutation continues: anchor % 1 is 0 and the padding AlignUp(delta, 1) - delta is 0, so it returns true with padding 0 as well.
The tail padding is less than the composite's alignment, a small power of two, so the conversion to int cannot overflow and the checked context never throws.

Only count zero with a positive element size newly reaches the body. The total is zero, remaining bytes and affordable bytes are nonnegative, both failure conditions stay false, and Take(0) returns an empty view without charging or moving. Cancellation is checked before either branch. Empty-span backing identity is unspecified; the supported result is the same empty element sequence and unchanged cursor/budget.

Only a null cause changes constructor selection. Both CStructReadException overloads delegate to the same protected constructor with ReadFailed, the same message and a null inner exception. The same Attach call follows, preserving category, message, field, path and offset.

ExitPointer's supported use returns from one successful unmatched EnterPointer, which pushes exactly one target before returning its resume position. Thus the stack contains at least one entry on every valid exit and both predicates pop the same target. LayoutEmitter.Arrays emits EnterPointer before its try and exactly one ExitPointer in finally, including nested targets. An extra exit without a matching entry violates the documented pairing and is not an equivalent-input claim.

unitSize is one or two. Every continuing chunk holds whole code units: a request is 256 bytes or the budget rounded down to whole units, a one-byte request is completed to a unit (or fails over budget), and a partial unit only occurs at the end of the input, which the zero-byte failure ends before alignment is computed again. Thus encodedByteCount is a multiple of unitSize whenever this expression is reached, its remainder is zero, and adding or subtracting that zero gives the same alignment.

At each reached alignment calculation encodedByteCount is a multiple of unitSize (every continuing chunk holds whole code units) and unitSize is one or two. The original inner remainder is zero; the replacement product is a multiple of unitSize, so the outer remainder remains zero. The count is bounded by an Int32-sized source, so its long product cannot overflow.

decoded is a private output-only scratch buffer passed to Decoder.Convert; its contents and output counts are never consumed. Decoder state is held by the separate decoder object, and the returned string is decoded independently from the original byte slice. Replacing the buffer adds allocations but changes no decoded result, consumption or failure.

Both Encoding.GetByteCount results are nonnegative Int32 values. The left operand is widened to Int64 before addition, so their sum is at most 2 * Int32.MaxValue, far below Int64.MaxValue. Removing checked from this sum cannot change overflow behavior, budget validation or the later allocation.

FixedDimensionSizes is called only from the multidimensional branches of the engine's reader and writer. CompileArrayShape rejects dependencies in every dimension of an array with more than one dimension, evaluates each count, and stores each result in CompiledArrayDimension.FixedCount. Peeling retains those fixed counts and placement preserves the array shape. Thus every multidimensional array reaching this helper has a non-null count for each dimension and a non-null total unless checked multiplication throws first. Changing only this unreachable missing-count message does not affect counts, overflow checks, decoding, writing or diagnostics.

UnionValue is sealed and implements IReadOnlyDictionary, not either mutable IDictionary interface inspected by WriteDataBinding.EnumerateMemberNames and TryGetMemberValue. Removing this early return therefore enumerates an empty name array; nested named fields also fail TryGetMemberValue without calling into the union value. Promoted composites recurse only over their finite inline declaration tree with that same unrecognized data object, reaching the same empty lookups. No caller callbacks, value validation or stream operations occur. WriteUnion still performs the actual union-name, storage-size and selected-member checks afterwards. This qualification does not apply to removing those validations.

This rethrow is inside catch (CStructException exception) when (exception.NoteMember(...)). The nonvirtual CStructException.NoteMember method attaches the innermost member context and unconditionally returns false. The exception therefore continues unwinding without entering this catch body. Removing its unreachable throw preserves the filter call, context attachment and original exception propagation. This qualification does not apply to the following conditional-scope CompleteField call or any cancellation checkpoint.

Every caller of SuppliesAnyPromotedMember (its own recursion and the compiled write engine's union selection) first requires membership in a compiled composite's PromotedFields set. That set contains only anonymous inline Struct declarations. CompileComposite resolves these declarations through compositeSymbols, completes and binds their CompiledCompositeType before publishing the parent model; the immutable field keeps that symbol. Thus promoted.Type.Symbol.Definition is always a CompiledCompositeType here, and the defensive non-composite return cannot execute. Changing only its boolean cannot affect recursive member selection.

The recursive promoted-member branch applies only to anonymous inline Struct declarations in PromotedFields. Their empty declaration names are preserved by effective-field compilation and placement. If recursion finds no supplied named leaf, removing this continue only reaches the next name.Length > 0 guard with an empty name. It short-circuits without consulting caller data and proceeds to the same next member. A successful recursion still returns true before this statement. The nonempty-name guard remains required and is not qualified by this proof.
